tools-ci.keepSummary: honest CI coverage and publication, trustworthy measurements, deterministic isolation, research provenance and safe preview tooling
protections: CI cannot turn missing history, a failed prerequisite or stale proof into a pass.
Preview publishing preserves the live site and other builders’ files.
Measurements compare equivalent inputs and distinguish missing telemetry from zero.
Interleaved worlds and settings preserve deterministic state and tuning fingerprints.
Research seeds, source identities and report denominators remain auditable.

groups.title: CI coverage, publication and proof guards
groups.question: Keep this group unchanged?
groups.reason: Parsed workflow YAML, tiny Git/command fixtures and stubbed pixels check fail-closed coverage, publication restrictions and current scheduling policy. world-audit parses strings; effects-scene tests a synthetic nonblank detector. Four shards and8px/32 are current operational rules rather than timeless invariants. No generated outcome target is run.
examples: cannot pass missing history or an empty diff as a related run
does not hide a failing selected test by rerunning the full suite
proof server resolves build identities and rejects encoded traversal without a local listener
exampleLabels: Missing history cannot produce a related-test pass.
A failed selected test stays failed.
Proof serving rejects encoded path traversal.

groups.title: Measurement and diagnostic contracts
groups.question: Keep this group unchanged?
groups.reason: Supplied traces, fake clocks/workers/GL and shader source tokens test honest telemetry, comparison boundaries and performance budgets. The30000 upload calls and256 masks are synthetic coverage, not game populations. Intentional shader changes may require a separately reviewed baseline; no replacing ruling was established.
examples: rejects an unmeasured API trip instead of counting missing telemetry as zero
preserves worker handlers, receiver, return values and transfer-list identity
does not extend pending-stage elapsed time through a transport backlog
exampleLabels: An unmeasured trip is not recorded as zero cost.
Transport backlog does not inflate stage time.

groups.title: Generated-world fingerprints and repeat-night isolation
groups.question: Keep this group unchanged?
groups.reason: These do step generated games (240/600-step paths plus short wave advances). Assertions compare matched state, semantic fingerprint sensitivity and reset behavior rather than wins, survival or kills. The historical15.605 file seconds remain integrity work, not a savings proposal.
examples: is the same for a knob added, a note edited, or the groups reordered: the tuning file is an input, not the state
the second night is the night played fresh
a new game puts the fight's settings back as a page starts them (the last night's are read before its first fight)
exampleLabels: Notes and unused knobs do not change the game fingerprint.
The second night equals a fresh matching night.
A new game resets previous fight settings.

groups.title: Research provenance and generated data
groups.question: Keep this group unchanged?
groups.reason: Most inputs are fabricated rows/configs. Screen tests validate frozen experiment controls and gate text, not whether a bot wins. Toy ask/tell scores protect resumability. Tiny real expert-contract cases assert provenance, replay equality and honest unsupported results. The inventory classifier tests pass strings like advance(world); they never advance a world. Newly added synthetic inventory cases have been reviewed by the integrator.
examples: external rows cannot leak held-out pairs or first-round reserved survey pairs
merge refuses duplicates, wrong cells, missing shards, missing progression and model drift
preserves enums, records, nullable values and optional keys without adding constraints
exampleLabels: Held-out and reserved seeds cannot leak into training rows.
Survey merges reject duplicate or missing work.
Generated types retain optional and nullable fields.

groups.title: Preview and visual-review tool integrity
groups.question: Keep this group unchanged?
groups.reason: Throwaway Git fixtures, small typed arrays/depth bits, stubbed wrappers and glyph/genome records prove safe tooling and opted-in comparisons. Deterministic shape/ink constants are readability rules, not night outcomes. Art/creature owners should confirm a future acceptance-constant change.
examples: adds only the named files, whatever is staged or missing in the checkout
keeps adjacent sampled float32 depths distinct instead of re-quantizing to DEPTH24
default-off and unknown switch preserve every production record by identity and hash
exampleLabels: Preview publishing adds only the named files.
Depth readback preserves distinct neighboring values.
An unused preview switch preserves production data.

groups.title: One mixed replay and fixture-sanity case
groups.question: Ask the report/combat owner to separate fixture-sanity predicates from this replay test? Yes opens a targeted follow-up review; deterministic replay and accounting stay blocking. It does not move or delete the case.
groups.reason: One declaration runs30/5s real cases plus stun fixtures15/30s. Repeated runs and phase accounting are hard integrity proofs; censored/stunned/hits>0/retaliation>0 predicates also validate the selected scenario. This is not a demonstrated pure outcome test to move wholesale. Exact purpose needs its report/combat owner.
examples: real-rules replay is deterministic across interleaved bots and bags
exampleLabels: Interleaved bots and bags replay deterministically.
